title: Path Prioritization Schema, Validator, and Gradual Shift Procedures
content:
Purpose:
This note captures the "path prioritization" routing rule schema we prototyping for multi-region control-plane routing, the validator invariants we need to prevent surprising traffic storms, and a conservative progressive-shift rollout procedure with safety gates. The aim is to enable expressive routing (conditions, weights, fallbacks, precedence) while keeping the validator simple enough for fast local checks and CI policy gates.

Context / Motivation:
- Current routing DSL mixes precedence and weight semantics and that has produced ambiguous configs in the wild. We want a small orthogonal schema that separates match predicates from distribution semantics (primary/weighted/fallback).
- Users require: predictable failover, regional affinity, and explicit canary windows across Dedicated and Hosted tiers.
- This doc is a working playbook: not final. Includes sample JSON/YAML shape and a minimal validator checklist to run in CI.

High-level design decisions (summary):
- Two-stage rule model: "match" -> "path action" (one of primary, weighted-set, fallback).
- Strong anti-overlap checks: no two rules at same precedence may both match identical request signatures.
- Explicit precedence number (lower = higher priority) to avoid implicit ordering semantics.
- Weight-based distributions are only allowed inside a single "weighted-set" action; weights are normalized and must sum > 0.
- Fallback chains limited to depth 3 to bound tail recursion and make reasoning simpler.

Sample JSON schema fragment (illustrative, validator should use canonicalized form):

{
  "rule_id": "string",
  "precedence": "integer (0..100)",
  "match": {
    "region": "optional string or list",
    "route_key": "optional string or regex",
    "headers": "optional map where values can be exact or prefix",
    "client_tier": "optional enum: [free, standard, enterprise]"
  },
  "action": {
    "type": "enum: [primary, weighted_set, fallback]",
    "primary_target": "model-id or route-id (when type==primary)",
    "weighted_targets": "list of {target, weight} (when type==weighted_set)",
    "fallback_target": "route-id or null (when type==fallback)"
  },
  "max_connections": "optional integer limit",
  "notes": "optional string"
}

Validator checks (static + semantic):
1) Schema linting: required fields present, types correct, no unknown keys.
2) Precedence range: 0..100. Lower numbers have higher priority; config should include doc comment explaining precedence.
3) Non-overlap at same precedence: for any two rules with equal precedence, assert their match predicates are not simultaneously satisfiable. Basic check: exact header+route+region overlaps should be detected; regex overlaps flagged for manual review.
4) Weight sanity: weighted_set weights must be positive ints and the sum must be > 0. Reject if any weight < 1.
5) Fallback chain depth <= 3 and no cycles. Use DFS on fallback graph and fail on cycle.
6) Region compatibility: if a rule references region(s) that currently have no provisioned capacity for the targeted model, validator emits WARNING with link to capacity matrix.
7) Safety caps: deny rules that set precedence=0 with large traffic surfaces unless explicitly flagged with "danger: true" and signed off.
8) Immutable target pins: when promoting in prod, ensure any target referenced is a pinned model-version (not :latest) unless the rule is marked non-pinned.

Semantic gates in CI (pre-promotion):
- Run the validator on the PR. Fail PR on any ERRORs; WARNs allowed but must be acknowledged.
- Run simulated coverage test: sample traffic generator runs match predicates against historical sampled keys to estimate affected QPS and % of routed traffic. Use that to populate expected shift percentages for rollout plan.
- Lint for disallowed constructs (eg. lookaround regex).

Rollout mechanics (conservative, observable):
Stages: dry-run -> staging -> canary (1%) -> canary (5%) -> ramp to 25% -> 50% -> 100%
- Dry-run: deploy rule as inactive, enable logging of what would have matched for 24h. Verify no unexpected matches in staging traffic.
- Staging: route internal traffic (dev, infra tests) through new rule for 1h walls. Confirm metrics.
- Canary windows: use timeboxed windows per step (typical: 15m for 1%, 30-60m for 5%, 1-2h for 25%).
- Ramp strategy: exponential or manual, but each step must be annotated with expected sample size and health thresholds.
- Abort conditions (any step):
  - Error rate increase > 2x baseline OR absolute error rate > 0.5% (adjust per service SLA).
  - 95th pct latency increase > 40% relative to baseline for the model/route.
  - Service-level SLI breach for downstream prepared systems.
  - Increase in model-generated safety flags (for chat/generation flows) beyond threshold.
On abort: automatic rollback to last healthy rule version, and create incident with auto-populated runbook links.

Automations and hooks:
- Validator plugin (go) used in CI to produce machine-readable failures and human-friendly explanations.
- Preflight simulator: offline tool that replays sampled trace and produces "delta QPS" and heatmap across regions.
- Canary controller: controller that updates traffic-splitting config based on approved plan and monitors metrics; exposes manual pause/rollback buttons in Console.
- Fallback auto-flip: if primary target loses capacity in region X, control plane can flip to first valid fallback with circuit-breaker cooldown (default 30s) and emit alert.

Observability signals to monitor during rollout:
- Routed QPS per rule_id, per target.
- Error rate (4xx/5xx) and exception class counts per target.
- Tail latency (95/99) per route and per model.
- Model quality signals (eval prompts, quality regression hooks) if enabled.
- Capacity headroom metrics and GPU queue lengths.
- Match-miss logs: cases where no rule matched (should be rare).

Testing matrix (minimum required):
- Unit tests for parser & schema (100% of branches where possible).
- Property tests for precedence semantics and weight normalization.
- Integration: simulated multi-region failover test (bring region A to zero capacity, assert fallback route used).
- Chaos: drop 30% of responses for a target during canary and verify auto-abort triggers.
- Load: small soak at 25% ramp for 2h to detect resource regressions.

Runbook snippets (two quick commands):
- Quick rollback: control-plane API: POST /v1/rules/{rule_id}/promote?to=previous-version (or UI rollback). Always include incident id in comment.
- Emergency disable: PATCH /v1/rules/{rule_id} { "action": { "type": "fallback", "fallback_target": "global-failover" } }

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should precedence be expanded to a richer boolean expression language for tie-breaking? Tradeoff: power vs validator complexity.
- Decide canonical naming for region sets vs placement groups.
- Implement an offline "overlap exactness" checker for regexes (could be costly). Plan: flag regex overlaps for manual review for now.
- Finalize default abort thresholds (work with SRE and product).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative in rollout cadence and validator strictness. We can relax after 6 months of safe runs.
- Please run the preflight simulator against a sample day of logs (see linked_artifacts) and paste output in PR.

References and links:
- capacity matrix: https://docs.internal/capacity-matrix (internal)
- CI validator prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/789
- Related design doc: confluence:route-priority-guidelines
